gloss: to be humid; to be stuffy; to steam

definitions.gloss: to be stuffy; to be humid and hot
definitions.explanation: When enclosed spaces or clothing become uncomfortably warm and humid.
When skin or body parts become hot and sweaty due to poor ventilation.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}は{靴|くつ}の{中|なか}が{蒸|む}れて{気持|きも}ち{悪|わる}い。
examples.english: In summer, my shoes get stuffy and uncomfortable.

examples.japanese: {蒸|む}れた{空気|くうき}で{息苦|いきぐる}しい。
examples.english: The humid air makes it hard to breathe.

examples.japanese: {窓|まど}を{閉|し}めきった{部屋|へや}は{蒸|む}れて{耐|た}えられなかった。
examples.english: The room with all the windows shut was so stuffy I couldn't stand it.

examples.japanese: マスクをしていると{顔|かお}が{蒸|む}れる。
examples.english: Wearing a mask makes my face get hot and stuffy.

examples.japanese: {長靴|ながぐつ}を{履|は}いていたら{足|あし}が{蒸|む}れた。
examples.english: My feet got sweaty from wearing rubber boots.

examples.japanese: {帽子|ぼうし}をかぶり{続|つづ}けると{頭|あたま}が{蒸|む}れて{痒|かゆ}くなる。
examples.english: If you keep wearing a hat, your head gets sweaty and itchy.

notes:
{蒸|む}れる is an intransitive verb ({自動詞|じどうし}). The transitive form is {蒸|む}らす (to steam, to let something get humid).

ASPECT ({ている}):
{蒸|む}れている indicates an ongoing state of being stuffy or humid.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {靴|くつ}が{蒸|む}れる - shoes get stuffy
- {部屋|へや}が{蒸|む}れる - room becomes stuffy
- {足|あし}が{蒸|む}れる - feet get sweaty
- {蒸|む}れた{暑|あつ}さ - humid heat

RELATED WORDS:
- {湿|しめ}る - to become damp (more general)
- {蒸|む}し{暑|あつ}い - muggy, sultry (adjective)
- {蒸|む}れる specifically implies uncomfortable heat and humidity combined
